Long-Tail Item Recommendation in Collaborative Filtering Framework

Abstract:

Recommender systems play a crucial role in providing personalized suggestions across domains such as e-commerce, education, and entertainment. Collaborative Filtering (CF), one of the most widely used recommendation techniques, suffers from popularity bias, where frequently interacted items are recommended more often, while long-tail items receive limited exposure due to sparse user interactions. &nbspThis thesis addresses the long-tail recommendation problem by proposing three novel approaches within the collaborative filtering framework. First, a graph-based recommendation model is developed by constructing an item&ndashitem interaction matrix and user-specific graphs, where entropy and inverse popularity measures improve the exposure of long-tail items. Second, a two-phase deep learning framework integrates a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) for rating imputation of long-tail items with a Graph Neural Network (GNN) to learn robust user and item representations from the enriched interaction graph. Finally, a multi-stage embedding refinement framework combines diffusion models, contrastive learning, and GNNs to enhance graph connectivity, improve embedding robustness, and alleviate the limitations of sparse interactions and unstable graph representations. Experimental evaluation on the MovieLens 100K and MovieLens 1M datasets demonstrates that the proposed methods consistently improve recommendation accuracy, long-tail recommendation quality, and catalog coverage while maintaining competitive overall recommendation performance.
